name: Gestao Hospital
description: We need an API to organize a public health system, specifically to assist the Unified Health System (SUS) in Brazil. The goal is to create a tool that helps avoid waste and optimize resources based on patient needs. The system should manage hospital information, including their stock of products, blood banks, and available beds. It should be able to recommend the closest hospital with available beds to a patient and facilitate the transfer of products, such as blood, between nearby hospitals if one is in need. A hospital with four or fewer items or liters of a product is considered to have only enough for its own use. The API should allow for registering hospitals, indicating the closest hospital to a patient's location, managing patient check-in and check-out, checking available beds, and managing product and blood bank inventories within hospitals.
highLevelGoals: The Public Health System Administrator aims to efficiently manage and distribute resources like hospital beds, medical products, and blood supplies to minimize waste and meet patient needs.
The Public Health System Administrator seeks to ensure patients are directed to the most suitable and closest hospitals with available resources, improving patient care and system efficiency.

The Public Health System Administrator aims to enable seamless and rapid transfer of critical resources, such as blood and medical products, between hospitals to address urgent needs and prevent shortages.
The Patient aims to quickly receive recommendations for the closest hospital with available beds when in need of medical attention.
The Patient expects their check-in and check-out processes to be managed efficiently and accurately within the public health system.
The Hospital Staff aims to accurately record and manage patient check-in and check-out information to ensure proper patient flow and bed utilization.
The Hospital Staff seeks to continuously monitor and update the availability of hospital beds to facilitate patient placement and resource allocation.
The Hospital Staff aims to efficiently manage and track the inventory of medical products and blood bank supplies to prevent shortages and ensure availability for patient care.
lowLevelGoals: The Public Health System Administrator can retrieve a comprehensive overview of current resource distribution across all public health facilities to identify areas of surplus and deficit.
The Public Health System Administrator can adjust the allocation of specific medical products to a hospital based on current demand and inventory levels.
The Public Health System Administrator can reallocate blood supplies from a hospital with surplus to one with critical need.
The Public Health System Administrator can generate a report detailing resource utilization trends over a specified period to inform future allocation strategies.
The Public Health System Administrator can identify the closest hospital with available beds for a patient based on their current location and medical needs.
The Public Health System Administrator can view a real-time map displaying bed availability across all hospitals in the system.
The Public Health System Administrator can assign a patient to a specific hospital and bed, updating the system accordingly.
The Public Health System Administrator can receive alerts when a hospital's bed occupancy reaches a critical threshold.
The Public Health System Administrator can initiate a transfer request for medical products from one hospital to another, specifying quantity and urgency.
The Public Health System Administrator can approve or reject pending resource transfer requests, providing reasons for rejection.
The Public Health System Administrator can track the real-time status and location of resources being transferred between hospitals.
The Public Health System Administrator can receive notifications upon successful completion or any delays in resource transfers.
The Patient can submit their current location to receive recommendations for the closest hospital with available beds.
The Patient can filter hospital recommendations based on specific medical services or specialties.
The Patient can view estimated wait times for recommended hospitals.
The Patient can confirm selection of a recommended hospital to initiate the check-in process.
The Patient can provide personal and medical information for check-in, ensuring accurate record-keeping.
The Patient can receive a digital confirmation of successful check-in, including assigned bed details.
The Patient can initiate the check-out process upon discharge.
The Patient can receive a summary of their stay and discharge instructions digitally.
The Hospital Staff can record a new patient's check-in details, including personal information and assigned bed.
The Hospital Staff can update a patient's check-out status and discharge date.
The Hospital Staff can retrieve a patient's complete check-in and check-out history.
The Hospital Staff can generate reports on patient flow and bed utilization rates.
The Hospital Staff can update the availability status of individual hospital beds (e.g., 'occupied', 'vacant', 'cleaning').
The Hospital Staff can view a real-time dashboard displaying the current bed occupancy for their hospital.
The Hospital Staff can mark a bed as 'unavailable' for maintenance or other reasons.
The Hospital Staff can receive alerts when the number of available beds falls below a predefined threshold.
The Hospital Staff can add new medical products to the hospital inventory, specifying quantity, expiry date, and location.
The Hospital Staff can update the quantity of existing medical products after usage or replenishment.
The Hospital Staff can record new blood donations, including blood type, donation date, and donor information.
The Hospital Staff can track the usage of blood products and update blood bank inventory accordingly.
The Hospital Staff can generate alerts for medical products or blood supplies nearing their expiry date or critical low stock levels.
